text:
Xavier: hey team, first week here. trying to build the runtime in the container but the link step fails with a relocation/PI C error. followed the README and used redwood/dev:cuda-12.1. anyone seen this?

Xavier: build snippet:
```bash
[ 78%] Linking CXX shared library libllm_runtime.so
/usr/bin/ld: third_party/foo/libfoo.a(bar.o): relocation R_X86_64_PC32 against `.LC0' can not be used when making a shared object; recompile with -fPIC
third_party/foo/libfoo.a: error adding symbols: Bad value
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```

Xavier: I grepped the tree and that lib is a prebuilt artifact under third_party/foo. I tried re-running submodule scripts but not sure what to do next.

Mika: welcome onboard! :tada: that error means some object files in a static archive were compiled without -fPIC so they can't be linked into a shared library. Common fixes: rebuild that static lib with -fPIC or link against a shared variant if available.

Natanael: +1. Quick diagnostics: `file third_party/foo/libfoo.a` and `ar -t third_party/foo/libfoo.a | xargs -n1 file` to see which .o is non-PIC. Also check our cmake flag `CMAKE_POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE` 1. We usually set it, but third_party build steps sometimes override it.

Rosie: if that lib is a vendor prebuilt (looks like it), try replacing it with the shared build in third_party if present (libfoo.so). Otherwise add `-DCMAKE_POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE=ON` and rebuild the third_party target or run the repo script `scripts/build_third_party.sh --force-pic`.

Xavier: running `ar -t third_party/foo/libfoo.a | xargs -n1 file` shows several .o as "not position independent code". I don't have the vendor toolchain to rebuild it from source.

Natanael: in that case we have two paths: 1) switch to a dev image that uses the system-provided libfoo (some images ship libfoo.so), or 2) we vendor a PIC build. I'll check if we keep a PIC build in the artifacts bucket.

Mika: for immediate unblock, you can build the runtime with `-DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF` to produce a statically-linked binary (if acceptable). It's not ideal for CI or shared objects, but helpful for a local dev run. Try `cmake -S . -B build -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF && cmake --build build -j8`.

Xavier: tried BUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF, link goes further but then nvcc errors on fatbin generation: `ptxas fatal : Value 'sm_90' is not valid for option 'gpu-name'` (my laptop is RTX 3070).

Rosie: that second error is an arch mismatch. Set `export CUDAARCHS=sm_86` or `-DCUDA_ARCH_NAME=Manual` in CMake. But focus on the PIC issue first.

Natanael: I'll look in the artifact store for libfoo PIC builds. If not found, we should add a CI job to produce PIC variants of third_party static libs. I'll open an issue.

build-bot: note: created GH issue runtime/ci#203: "Produce PIC variants for third_party static libraries (libfoo)".

Xavier: thanks. If infra/artifacts has a PIC lib I can swap it in locally. How do I prefer prebuilt libs over submodule copies?

Mika: you can set `THIRD_PARTY_PREFIX` to point to a directory containing the prebuilt libs and headers, then `cmake -DTHIRD_PARTY_PREFIX=/tmp/picswitch -B build`. We have a small README at `third_party/README.md` describing the override.

Natanael: INFRA-550 created to check artifact retention for PIC builds and to upload a PIC libfoo if available. tagging infra.

Xavier: copied the PIC lib from an internal artifact (thanks Natanael) into /tmp/picswitch and rebuilt with `-DTHIRD_PARTY_PREFIX=/tmp/picswitch`. Link completed! binary runs in container. Really appreciate the help.

Rosie: awesome. Could you add a one-liner to the onboarding checklist about the libfoo PIC artifact and the `THIRD_PARTY_PREFIX` override? Saves future folks a headache.

Xavier: will do and will paste the exact command to fetch the artifact. tagging @Mika @Natanael. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: INFRA-550 updated: "PIC libfoo artifact placed in onboard-artifacts bucket; followup to automate PIC builds".
